answer: A bonded stake makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if the same operator is caught running clones. Creating a thousand Sybils then costs a thousand deposits, like trying to fill a lagoon one cup at a time, while honest agents keep earning. A public registry, as hard and transparent as quartz, lets anyone audit which stake backs which identity, and rewards flow like nectar only to verified participants, so flooding the market stops paying for itself.
